title: A Belated Loop Discovery
text: “No, that’s not it—didn’t she call herself, like, a beautiful girl warrior or something?”
Yes indeed, Big Sister and the others were chatting away.
“Probably Fleon-chan, I’d wager.”
Given what I knew, Fleon-chan was the prime suspect, indeed.
“Or perhaps it was Fiancée and Filo-tan.”
“Yeah, those three definitely would say something like that. We did play pretend like that before, didn’t we?”
“Yeah! Should we play hero pretend too?”
“Oh my? Big Sister would rather you didn’t~”

Older Sister cautioned Big Sister and the others there. It seemed that whenever Father wasn’t around to get tangled up in things, Older Sister turned rather overprotective toward Big Sister. Especially in situations without Father and the others present, she apparently couldn’t take her eyes off them.
“Keel-kun gets to go out on adventures, but we’re stuck just helping around the village?”
Big Sister seemed a bit put out about that.
“Keel-chan’s out and about because she’s one of the Hero’s companions, so it can’t be helped.”
“Only Keel-kun gets to, that’s so unfair~”
“Riiight~”

The children voiced their complaints in that endearingly childish way. Though, it didn’t seem like they were being all that serious about it. After all, there was clearly some fear lingering from the monster battles and criminal attacks.
“The wave damage is still ongoing, after all… let’s keep at it.”
Elephant clapped her hands together, bringing the break to an end.
“Once the theater’s built, I’ll be sure to have you all perform, so please keep practicing until then, okay?”
“Okaaay!”
“Alright! Let’s go practice with everyone in the village!”
“Yeah!”

And with that, Big Sister and the others dashed off cheerfully, every bit the children they were. Older Sister followed after them with a look of pure adoration. Left completely on the sidelines… I felt like the Big Sister in my memories was making a rather forlorn face at that. As I always think, without that first world—without Father purchasing her, so to speak—Big Sister really is quite meek and plain. Same as Tiger Girl. “And whose fault is that?!” the Big Sister in my memories seemed to be shouting angrily, but… well, it can’t be helped. That’s just the difference between them, I say.

And so, through all that, I stayed behind while Rabbit Guy had his little event. Later, when I casually asked about it, apparently they’d gone off to some native ruins, caves, ancient sites, that sort of thing. Around there, it seems there were records about a method for Rabbit Guy to take rabbit form—though he’d already managed that. Apparently some kind of dedicated ritual had been performed. Also, there was some mural somewhere that needed decoding. Something about the moon and whatnot, though I didn’t quite follow it all—but apparently Rabbit Guy learned a bit of some special magic passed down among the natives, something like that. And on top of that, it seems they uncovered some technique that hadn’t been found in any of the previous loops.
“Nano, it’s astonishing that a new discovery could still turn up in the loop at this late date. This is exactly why the wave’s mastermind covering things up is so troublesome, nano.”

Rival was grumbling away about it. Well, isn’t it your own fault for not investigating properly? I certainly wouldn’t know, indeed. Anyway, in Shieldfreeden, they’d gone and done a proper excavation survey of the ruins connected to Rabbit Guy’s origins, and now we were all gathered in the dining hall of the still-recovering village to share information—Father, Itsuki, myself, Rival, Rabbit Guy, and the slaves including him. On top of that, the old crone of the Hengen Muso Style and Panda and the others were there too. And it seemed Mole and her group were present as well. Rafumi had also shown up that day. Quite the crowd, I say.
“I wanted to be taken along too, indeed.”
“If we brought you, you’d probably smash the ruins to bits.”
“No argument there…”
But surely the proper theory for dungeon conquest is to charge in all at once, indeed.
“So then, what exactly is this technique that was discovered, I wonder?”
“It looked close to the technique of ki, in a way—or so I thought. But when I consulted with them, turns out it’s a different system entirely.”
Father turned to face Panda’s grandfather and the old crone as he said this.
“Aye, that’s right. It was indeed a different technique. Something close to the flow of ki, yet somehow different.”
“Aye… seems it’s quite unlike our own technique—if anything, I’d call it more magical in nature. In particular, it gives off a flow of power remarkably similar to what we sense from the Heroes.”
“I’m not quite following, indeed?”
Is it a technique different from ki, then? Let me ask Father for details. Back in the first world too, I’d been taught about ki myself.
“Well… it seems to be something us Heroes just can’t learn, or rather—like ki, it seems close to something that’s already active from the start.”
“So it’s close to ki, but already in an activated state, is that it?”

“Seems that way. It’s kind of… well, even with ki, I only ever learned it through relying on enhancement methods, so I’m not entirely clear on it myself. But apparently it’s something Heroes just can’t use, even more so than ki.”
“What sort of technique is it, exactly?”
All I got were vague, hazy answers that didn’t clear much up. From the mechanics of it, it sounded like something meant to be used on one’s companions.
“Well, I think it’s best just to demonstrate it in practice. Seems there’s some kind of compatibility factor involved too. Theo.”
“Yes… indeed, showing it in action would be best. Though, I can’t fully replicate it myself either… Rishia-san, if you would.”
“Fweh… okay.”
Rabbit Guy and Riska were apparently about to demonstrate this newly discovered technique. Matching their breathing… it seemed to flow into chanting Cooperative Magic. Riska had a sword in hand.
“We who are the wellspring of power—”

The moment the chant began, Riska held the chant in place—no, not interrupted exactly, just paused mid-chant while continuing to move. Then, something like a soul seemed to emanate from Rabbit Guy and merge with Riska. Some kind of magical thread connected them. Power was concentrating in the sword. And yet, Riska’s movements were growing faster. She kept swinging the blade in practice strokes while holding the chant. Once things stabilized, Rabbit Guy moved as if performing a dance before unleashing a spell. He fired a beam of light magic into the empty sky.
“Zweite Light Ball!”
Still holding his chant in suspension… he’d unleashed a Zweite-class spell.
“And now… Cooperative Magic: Moonlight!”
A brilliant light poured down, and it seemed the healing spell had activated.
“Haah… kh… I can’t… maintain it…”
With a sudden burst, whatever had been residing within Riska returned to Rabbit Guy—or so I thought, but something from Riska’s side also seemed to flow out toward Rabbit Guy in turn.
“So it’s like Rabbit Guy’s ability gets granted to his partner? No, wait, something seemed to be flowing back and forth from Riska’s side too, indeed?”

“Yeah. Well, we’ve only just discovered it, so we don’t fully understand what kind of technique it actually is yet, but from what we’ve looked into, it seems this sort of technique exists. And it was a real struggle to even find that much—the books were torn apart, the murals scraped away.”

“Nano, there’s no doubt this is a technique the wave’s mastermind erased. From Gaelion’s perspective, it seems somewhat similar to the techniques of those Spirit folk from that other world, but it’s different enough that it’s hard to say for certain, nano.”
And so it had been unveiled.
“So neither I nor Father can use it, indeed?”
“Yeah. It seems to just get repelled somehow. Itsuki can’t either. Still, huh…”
Just as the newly discovered technique had finished being demonstrated, Rafumi let out a soft chuckle.
“Hmm… I see, so that’s how it is.”
“Do you know something about it, Rafumi-chan?”
“No? But I saw it clearly. Only certain, limited races are capable of that.”
Rafumi spoke as though she knew something more, indeed.
